name: userfaultfd-open
why: userfaultfd(O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK) is the rare timing-primitive syscall the rule anchors on
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for userfaultfd_behavioral.c's userfaultfd() record (flags 0x80800)

name: userfaultfd-noflags
why: userfaultfd(0) with no flags from a differently named tool is the same syscall anchor; the flag bits must not hide it
source: synthetic: an exploit PoC calling userfaultfd(0)

name: uffdio-register-ioctl
why: UFFDIO_REGISTER is an ioctl() on the uffd, the step the atomic issues right after userfaultfd(); it keeps the userfaultfd surface but is not the anchored syscall, so syscall==userfaultfd must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: ioctl(uffd, UFFDIO_REGISTER) following a userfaultfd()

name: mmap-not-userfaultfd
why: mmap(MAP_ANONYMOUS) is the companion allocation the atomic performs; an anonymous mmap is ubiquitous and benign, so the rule must key on the userfaultfd syscall, not the surrounding memory calls
source: synthetic: mmap of the anonymous region registered with the uffd

name: unrelated-close
why: an ordinary close(): a sanity floor that proves the userfaultfd selection does not fire on noise
